--- grub.cfg (bootupd)
# Generated by bootupd / do not edit

# This file is copied from https://github.com/coreos/coreos-assembler/blob/0eb25d1c718c88414c0b9aedd19dc56c09afbda8/src/grub.cfg
# Changes:
#   - Dropped Ignition glue, that can be injected into platform.cfg
# petitboot doesn't support -e and doesn't support an empty path part
if [ -d (md/md-boot)/grub2 ]; then
  # fcct currently creates /boot RAID with superblock 1.0, which allows
  # component partitions to be read directly as filesystems.  This is
  # necessary because transposefs doesn't yet rerun grub2-install on BIOS,
  # so GRUB still expects /boot to be a partition on the first disk.
  #
  # There are two consequences:
  # 1. On BIOS and UEFI, the search command might pick an individual RAID
  #    component, but we want it to use the full RAID in case there are bad
  #    sectors etc.  The undocumented --hint option is supposed to support
  #    this sort of override, but it doesn't seem to work, so we set $boot
  #    directly.
  # 2. On BIOS, the "normal" module has already been loaded from an
  #    individual RAID component, and $prefix still points there.  We want
  #    future module loads to come from the RAID, so we reset $prefix.
  #    (On UEFI, the stub grub.cfg has already set $prefix properly.)
  set boot=md/md-boot
  set prefix=($boot)/grub2
else
  if [ -f ${config_directory}/bootuuid.cfg ]; then
    source ${config_directory}/bootuuid.cfg
  fi
  if [ -n "${BOOT_UUID}" ]; then
    search --fs-uuid "${BOOT_UUID}" --set boot --no-floppy
  else
    search --label boot --set boot --no-floppy
  fi
fi
set root=$boot

if [ -f ${config_directory}/grubenv ]; then
  load_env -f ${config_directory}/grubenv
elif [ -s $prefix/grubenv ]; then
  load_env
fi

if [ -f $prefix/console.cfg ]; then
  # Source in any GRUB console settings if provided by the user/platform
  source $prefix/console.cfg
fi

menuentry_id_option="--id"

function load_video {
  insmod all_video
}

set timeout_style=menu
set timeout=1

# Other package code will be injected from here

### BEGIN 01_users.cfg ###
# Keep the comment for grub2-set-password
### BEGIN /etc/grub.d/01_users ###
if [ -f ${prefix}/user.cfg ]; then
  source ${prefix}/user.cfg
  if [ -n "${GRUB2_PASSWORD}" ]; then
    set superusers="root"
    export superusers
    password_pbkdf2 root ${GRUB2_PASSWORD}
  fi
fi
### END 01_users.cfg ###

### BEGIN 10_blscfg.cfg ###
# Hearth on Peppermint/Debian: Debian's signed GRUB has no `blscfg` command (Fedora's does), so the boot entries
# come from the menu /usr/libexec/nimbus/hearth-bls-grub writes next to this file from ostree's
# /boot/loader/entries. (Replaces bootupd's own 10_blscfg.cfg, which only says `blscfg`.)
if [ -f ${prefix}/hearth-bls.cfg ]; then
  source ${prefix}/hearth-bls.cfg
elif [ -f ($boot)/grub2/hearth-bls.cfg ]; then
  source ($boot)/grub2/hearth-bls.cfg
else
  menuentry 'Hearth OS: no boot entries yet (the installer must run hearth-bls-grub)' {
    echo "No /boot/grub2/hearth-bls.cfg: run /usr/libexec/nimbus/hearth-bls-grub --boot <the installed /boot>"
    sleep 15
  }
fi
### END 10_blscfg.cfg ###

### BEGIN 14_menu_show_once.cfg ###
# Force the menu to be shown once, with a timeout of ${menu_show_once_timeout}
# if requested by ${menu_show_once_timeout} being set in the env.
if [ "${menu_show_once_timeout}" ]; then
  set timeout_style=menu
  set timeout="${menu_show_once_timeout}"
  unset menu_show_once_timeout
  save_env menu_show_once_timeout
fi
### END 14_menu_show_once.cfg ###

### BEGIN 30_uefi-firmware.cfg ###
if [ "$grub_platform" = "efi" ]; then
        menuentry 'UEFI Firmware Settings' $menuentry_id_option 'uefi-firmware' {
                fwsetup
        }
fi
### END 30_uefi-firmware.cfg ###

### BEGIN 41_custom.cfg ###
if [ -f $prefix/custom.cfg ]; then
  source $prefix/custom.cfg
fi
### END 41_custom.cfg ###
--- hearth-bls.cfg
# Written by hearth-bls-grub from /run/hearth-install/target/boot/loader/entries: don't edit, it's rewritten on every update.
set default=0
menuentry 'Hearth OS (Debian 13)' --class hearth --class gnu-linux --id 'ostree-1' {
  load_video
  set gfxpayload=keep
  linux /ostree/default-dab27ef0f0b1613a166271ee1df189bf90df099e89769b3fdaa2ac972fc77db0/vmlinuz-7.2.12+deb13-amd64 root=UUID=27400e8d-ce3e-4245-89ff-2b844217e4fd rootflags=subvol=root rw ostree=/ostree/boot.1/default/dab27ef0f0b1613a166271ee1df189bf90df099e89769b3fdaa2ac972fc77db0/0 quiet splash loglevel=3 nvidia-drm.modeset=1 nvidia-drm.fbdev=1 systemd.gpt_auto=0 rd.systemd.gpt_auto=0 console=ttyS0,115200 plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles
  initrd /ostree/default-dab27ef0f0b1613a166271ee1df189bf90df099e89769b3fdaa2ac972fc77db0/initramfs-7.2.12+deb13-amd64.img 
}
if [ -f "${prefix}/hearth-theme.cfg" ]; then source "${prefix}/hearth-theme.cfg"; fi
--- hearth-theme.cfg
# Written by hearth-bls-grub: Hearth's look for this menu. Sourced after every entry is in the menu; if anything
# here is missing or fails, GRUB keeps its plain text menu and starts exactly the same way.
if [ -f "${prefix}/themes/hearth/theme.txt" ]; then
  if insmod gfxterm; then
    if insmod gfxmenu; then
      if insmod png; then
        set hearth_font_ok=0
        for f in ${prefix}/themes/hearth/*.pf2; do
          if [ -f "$f" ]; then
            if loadfont "$f"; then set hearth_font_ok=1; fi
          fi
        done
        if [ "${hearth_font_ok}" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -z "${gfxmode}" ]; then set gfxmode=auto; fi
          if terminal_output gfxterm; then
            set theme="${prefix}/themes/hearth/theme.txt"
            export theme
          fi
        fi
      fi
    fi
  fi
fi
